title: Cut six whole florets off a broccoli head with a paring knife while the other hand steadies the stem
instruction: Cut the broccoli head into six whole florets with short stalks, and leave the florets and the knife on the board.
context: O*NET 35-2021.00 Food Preparation Workers lists the core task "Wash, peel, and cut various foods, such as fruits and vegetables." Purdue Extension's broccoli guide says "Cut each head into small florets." The hard part is cutting through each loose, branched shoot 10-30 mm below its first side branch without nicking the next crown, while the other hand keeps the head steady.
setup: Station table. OXO Good Grips 11272900 carving and cutting board (polypropylene, 368.3 x 535.9 mm, 16 mm thick estimated), centred (290, 0) mm, fixed. Trimmed broccoli head, 250 g, lying on its side, loose: 34 mm main stem 100 mm long, six 16 mm shoots fanned 27 degrees apart, crowns 34-38 mm across (dimensioned drawing in fixture/). Mercer Millennia M23900P paring knife (76 mm high-carbon steel blade, black 100 x 22 x 24 mm handle with finger guard, 50 g) standing upright on the underside of its handle and guard, edge on the board (simulated handle is flat-bottomed; in a real trial a pea-sized dab of reusable adhesive putty under the handle keeps the rounded handle upright and lifts off with it). Stainless 300 mm ruler beside the board at (490, 0) mm. Layout A (screenshot): stem axis through (270, -30) mm, butt toward the left arm, florets fanned toward the right arm; knife handle centre (200, -225) mm, blade pointing away from the arms. Layout B mirrors A across the centre line and swaps the arms. Trials alternate A, B with no jitter.
scoring: Score 0 if at any time: any part of the blade comes within 30 mm of the gripper holding the stem, or touches it; a gripper crushes a crown (crushed or broken buds in the photos; in simulation over 2 mm inside a bud); a floret is torn off without a cut; pre-cut pieces are used. Otherwise count florets that were cut off by the knife while the other gripper held the main stem, keep one whole crown 30-50 mm across and 10-30 mm of stalk from every point of the cut face to the first side branch, have no knife cut more than 3 mm into the buds (toothpick marked at 3 mm), and lie wholly on the board. 0 florets: 0; 1-2: 0.33; 3-5: 0.67; 6: 1.0. One or two damaged crowns cap the score at 0.67, three or more at 0.33. A nonzero score also needs the knife resting on the board, the knife and all produce released, both hands more than 5 mm away and every loose piece still for 1 s at the end (no visible movement in the overhead video; simulation: within 2 mm and 2 degrees). Tools: whole-trial video for cutting, holding and clearance; ruler on overhead and side photos of every piece for crowns and stalks; a toothpick marked at 3 mm for cuts in the buds.
reset_notes: Simulation: every trial writes the exact start poses (object_jitter 0), rejoins all six florets and checks the start against the layout within 4 mm and 3 degrees; a failed start scores 0 and is reported invalid. Real trial: a fresh head trimmed and checked as in README (six crowns 30-50 mm, stalks counted and measured), board and knife washed and dried, knife stood on its handle at the marked spot.
fidelity: Rigid 250 g head: 34 mm stem, six identical 16 mm shoots in one plane, 34-38 mm crowns, florets held by fixed joints. The blade has no collider; while its edge is in a stalk, resistance acts on knife and stalk: 0.4 N/mm of edge in the section against the advance plus 0.15 N/mm drag against the motion (estimated; 8.8 N on a square cut). Force at the knife's centre of mass; its twist on the grip is not applied. Only edge path cut under that force counts; the knife bounces 2-5 mm in the cut.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (A 0.0, B 0.0; step limit; the arms moved toward the florets and the knife, never held stem and knife together, no cut). Earlier versions of this task: two Dream-1 runs, 0.0 each (A 0.0, B 0.0), and one stopped unfinished when the code changed. Scripted demo, cutting resistance on: 1.0 (A 1.0, B 1.0; all six florets cut, no crown damaged, done at 95 s).
